facts.fact_text: Immediately after the announcement of the preliminary results of the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election, the applicant called on his supporters to gather at Freedom Square in central Yerevan.

The applicant called on his supporters to gather at Freedom Square in central Yerevan in order to protest against irregularities which had allegedly occurred in the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election process.
From 20 February 2008 onwards, nationwide daily protest rallies were held by the applicant's supporters.
The main meeting place of the applicant's supporters during the post-election protest rallies from 20 February 2008 onwards was Freedom Square and the surrounding park in Yerevan.
The rallies at Freedom Square were held during the daytime and late into the night, and attracted at times tens of thousands of people.
Several hundred demonstrators stayed at Freedom Square around the clock, having set up a camp.
The applicant participated in the post-election rallies in his capacity as opposition leader and presidential candidate.
The applicant gave speeches two to three times a day on issues of political and public interest during the post-election rallies.
The applicant regularly called on his supporters to continue the mass protests during the post-election rallies.
The applicant stayed at Freedom Square around the clock during the post-election rallies, leaving only for two to three hours a day.

The applicant alleged that he addressed the demonstrators from a platform at Freedom Square, saying: "We see that police forces have arrived on the square. Please, do not have any contact with them and do not touch them. Please, keep your distance from them. Let us wait and see what they want from us. If they have something to tell us, we are ready to listen. Please, be patient and peaceful".
The applicant alleged that the demonstrators followed his request and kept their distance from the police forces.

The Report of the Council of Europe Commissioner for Human Rights on his Special Mission to Armenia (CommDH(2008)11REV, 20 March 2008) stated that demonstrators started resisting and clashes broke out between the police and security forces and the demonstrators.

The Human Rights Watch Report (February 2009) stated that some demonstrators appeared ready to fight the police, which was why, according to the applicant, he urged the crowd not to resist the police.
The applicant alleged that suddenly, without any prior warning or orders to disperse, the police forces, shouting loudly, attacked the demonstrators at Freedom Square.
The applicant alleged that the police forces violently beat the demonstrators with rubber batons and destroyed the camp at Freedom Square.
The applicant alleged that in a matter of minutes the demonstrators were pushed out of Freedom Square.

The applicant alleged that while he was on the platform at Freedom Square, he was approached by the Head of the State Protection Department (SPD) of the National Security Service, who was also the chief of the Armenian President's bodyguard team, and other SPD officers.
The applicant alleged that the Head of the SPD and other SPD officers surrounded the applicant and his bodyguards and then forcibly took them to one of the central statues on Freedom Square.
The applicant alleged that after Freedom Square was cleared of all demonstrators, the Head of the SPD approached the applicant and ordered him to leave the square.
The applicant alleged that after further attempts to make him leave Freedom Square failed, the Head of the SPD forced the applicant into a car and took him to his house in Yerevan.
The applicant alleged that once at his house in Yerevan, he was not allowed to leave the territory of his house and garden.
The applicant alleged that the roads to his house were blocked by special police forces, SPD officers, the road traffic police and other police units.
The applicant alleged that no one could reach him or go in or out of his home without the permission of the special forces.

The applicant alleged that the special forces, after carrying out a search of visitors and their vehicles, reported their identity and the purpose of their visit to an unidentified superior and allowed visitors to go in and out only after receiving instructions from that person.

The SPD statement broadcast on 1 March 2008 stated that SPD officers had decided to remove the applicant from Freedom Square pursuant to Section 6 § 3 of the Act on Ensuring the Security of Persons Subject to Special State Protection, in order to ensure his safety as a former President of Armenia subject to State protection.

The SPD statement broadcast on 1 March 2008 stated that the applicant had been removed from Freedom Square and taken to his house, which was similarly to be protected by the SPD pursuant to Section 12 (2) of the Act on Ensuring the Security of Persons Subject to Special State Protection.

The SPD statement broadcast on 1 March 2008 stated that the SPD had warned the applicant that he must categorically refrain from attempting to leave his house, indicating that otherwise the SPD could not bear responsibility for his safety, since they could not accompany him to an unlawful demonstration.
The applicant alleged that his house arrest lasted without interruption until at least 20 March 2008.

The Report of the Council of Europe Monitoring Committee (Doc. 11579, 15 April 2008) stated that Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan (the applicant) was placed under de facto house arrest during the police action on 1 March 2008.

The Report of the Council of Europe Monitoring Committee (Doc. 11579, 15 April 2008) noted in a footnote that the authorities said the applicant was free to travel if he rescinded his security detail, but that the clearly existing threats to his personal safety and life made it impossible for him to do so, as was obviously known by the authorities.

The Report of the Council of Europe Commissioner for Human Rights on his Special Mission to Armenia (CommDH(2008)11REV, 20 March 2008) stated that former President Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan (the applicant) was held in what must be qualified as de facto house arrest.
The Human Rights Watch Report (February 2009) stated that the applicant (Levon Ter-Petrosyan) was subsequently taken home and effectively put under house arrest.

Section 1 of the Armenian Act on Ensuring the Security of Persons Subject to Special State Protection (2004) lists the main concepts used in the Act, including "protected objects", defined as buildings, constructions, structures, adjacent territories and transportation means where persons subject to State protection are permanently or temporarily located and which require protection in order to ensure the security of persons subject to State protection.

Section 6 § 3 of the Armenian Act on Ensuring the Security of Persons Subject to Special State Protection (2004) provides that a former President of Armenia is provided with personal lifetime State protection, except in cases prescribed by law.

Section 10 of the Armenian Act on Ensuring the Security of Persons Subject to Special State Protection (2004) provides that the authority carrying out State protection is the State Protection Department of Armenia.

Section 11(2) of the Armenian Act on Ensuring the Security of Persons Subject to Special State Protection (2004) lists as a main task of the State Protection Department of Armenia ensuring the security of persons subject to State protection at their permanent or temporary location, including during travel.

Section 11(7) of the Armenian Act on Ensuring the Security of Persons Subject to Special State Protection (2004) lists as a main task of the State Protection Department of Armenia ensuring the regime of access control established at a protected object.

Section 12(2) of the Armenian Act on Ensuring the Security of Persons Subject to Special State Protection (2004) provides that the State Protection Department of Armenia is obliged to organise and implement protective, regime, technical and other measures aimed at ensuring the security of persons subject to State protection.

Section 13(4) of the Armenian Act on Ensuring the Security of Persons Subject to Special State Protection (2004) provides that the State Protection Department of Armenia has the right to check the identity documents of public officials and other persons during their entry and exit to and from a protected object, to carry out their inspection and an inspection of objects which they have on them, their transportation means and objects transported in them, including by applying technical measures.

Section 14 § 1(4) of the Armenian Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (2004-2011) provides that the police are entitled to decide to terminate a public event and to order the organisers to terminate the event, by allowing them a reasonable time-limit to do so, if, after a warning by the police, public order and requirements of the law continue to be violated and this poses a real risk to the life and health of others, State and public security and public order, and may cause substantial pecuniary damage to the State, the community, natural or legal persons.

The SPD statement broadcast on 1 March 2008 stated that SPD officers had decided to remove the applicant from Freedom Square pursuant to Section 6 § 3 of the Act on Ensuring the Security of Persons Subject to Special State Protection, in order to ensure his safety as a former President of Armenia subject to State protection.

The SPD statement broadcast on 1 March 2008 stated that the applicant had been removed from Freedom Square and taken to his house, which was similarly to be protected by the SPD pursuant to Section 12 (2) of the Act on Ensuring the Security of Persons Subject to Special State Protection.

The SPD statement broadcast on 1 March 2008 stated that the SPD had warned the applicant that he must categorically refrain from attempting to leave his house, indicating that otherwise the SPD could not bear responsibility for his safety, since they could not accompany him to an unlawful demonstration.
On 4 March 2008 the General Prosecutor's Office replied that there was no such concept as "house arrest" under Armenian law.

The Human Rights Watch Report (February 2009) stated that according to multiple witnesses, the police made no audible demand for anyone to disperse nor gave any indication of the purpose of their presence at Freedom Square.

The Government alleged that the reason for the police operation of 1 March 2008 at Freedom Square was information obtained the day before by the law enforcement authorities, according to which a large number of weapons were to be distributed to the protesters to incite provocative actions and mass disorder in Yerevan.
The Government alleged that members of the relevant police force arrived on Freedom Square at around 7 a.m. on 1 March 2008 to verify information about weapons being distributed to protesters.
The Government alleged that the police met with resistance from the demonstrators at Freedom Square, who attacked the police officers with wooden bats, metal rods and stones.
The Government alleged that once violence had erupted on Freedom Square, the applicant was surrounded on the platform by the Head of the SPD and other SPD officers because his security was in danger.

The Government alleged that later in the afternoon of 1 March 2008, additional SPD and police forces were stationed near the applicant's house as part of special security measures employed in respect of all persons under State protection, because of the escalating violence in Yerevan.

The Government alleged that for security reasons SPD officers were instructed to search everyone entering the applicant's house, but were never instructed to prohibit anyone from entering the house or to prevent the applicant from leaving.

The Report of the Council of Europe Commissioner for Human Rights on his Special Mission to Armenia (CommDH(2008)11REV, 20 March 2008) stated that during the search operation at Freedom Square, tents were taken down and people were beaten and injured.

The Report of the Council of Europe Commissioner for Human Rights on his Special Mission to Armenia (CommDH(2008)11REV, 20 March 2008) stated that demonstrators started resisting and clashes broke out between the police and security forces and the demonstrators.

The Report of the Council of Europe Commissioner for Human Rights on his Special Mission to Armenia (CommDH(2008)11REV, 20 March 2008) stated that according to both parties, a tentative agreement seems to have been reached later on the morning of 1 March 2008 to relocate the demonstration and allow it to continue, either in front of the Myasnikyan monument near the French Embassy or close to the main train station.

The Report of the Council of Europe Commissioner for Human Rights on his Special Mission to Armenia (CommDH(2008)11REV, 20 March 2008) stated that the tentative agreement to relocate the demonstration appears never to have been properly communicated to the demonstrators by their leaders, notably Mr Ter-Petrosyan (the applicant), who at that stage was prevented from leaving his residence.
